Assessment
81-year-old female (MRN SYN-5506238) referred for 3 months of worsening right anterolateral thigh pain (now present at night) and intermittent left thigh ache, coexisting moderate right hip osteoarthritis, and a mail-order pharmacy renewal request for alendronate 70 mg weekly.

1. Cause of Pain - Incomplete Atypical Femoral Fracture (AFF) vs. Hip Osteoarthritis:
The patient's primary pain is NOT explained by her moderate right hip osteoarthritis. She localizes her dull, aching pain to the right anterolateral mid-thigh rather than the groin, has lateral mid-thigh tenderness on palpation, and hip internal rotation on orthopedic exam did not reproduce her primary pain. Critically, the 2024-04-26 radiology addendum to the 2024-04-22 right hip/pelvis radiograph identified new focal lateral cortical thickening (beaking) of the proximal right femoral shaft in the subtrochanteric region (~5 cm below the lesser trochanter).
